title: Hazel and the Colony
premise: Felix Montrose smuggles memories in her ship's cold vaults between the warring worlds of Kestrel and Vane, keeping her head down and her cargo unregistered. When gravity stutters for nine seconds system-wide, she finds a dying courier's implant fused to her own neural lace — carrying a decryption key that can either end the war or arm the final strike. Hunted by both governments and shadowed by the ragtag 'colony' of outcasts she's accidentally collected along the way, Felix must choose between destroying the key to stay safe or delivering it to the one place no one expects: the neutral station where the war began. She delivers it, the truth of who started the war goes public, and Felix finally accepts that her found family is worth more than her invisibility.
about_author: Rosalind Eastwick is the pen name of a former orbital logistics analyst who spent a decade writing technical manuals before turning to fiction. She lives near a decommissioned launch site and writes about people who carry heavy things across long distances.

chapters.title: Nine Seconds of Silence
chapters.summary: POV Felix. Running contraband memories past Kestrel customs, Felix feels gravity flicker for exactly nine seconds — her tea floats, her instruments scream. The beat is unease: the universe just noticed her.

chapters.title: The Courier Who Wouldn't Die
chapters.summary: POV Felix. A drifting escape pod holds a courier whose neural lace has burned out, fused with a data shard. Against instinct, Felix takes him aboard. Emotional beat: reluctant compassion overwriting self-preservation.

chapters.title: Cold Vault Confessions
chapters.summary: POV Felix. The courier, Ilya, half-lucid, tells her the shard carries a war-ending key — and that both fleets will kill for it. Beat: dread as Felix realizes her quiet route is now a battlefield.

chapters.title: The Colony Assembles
chapters.summary: POV Felix. At a fuel depot she picks up three strays: a disgraced Kestrel navigator, a Vane deserter medic, and an AI-salvager kid named Wren. Beat: warmth sneaking past Felix's armor; the 'colony' forms by accident.

chapters.title: Customs at Broken Anchor
chapters.summary: POV Wren. A checkpoint inspection nearly exposes Ilya in the hold. Wren improvises a forgery that saves them. Beat: first trust between strangers pretending to be family.

chapters.title: What the Shard Whispers
chapters.summary: POV Felix. The shard begins leaking fragments into Felix's own lace — images of the war's first day. She sees something impossible: a third party fired first. Beat: vertigo of inherited memory.

chapters.title: Kestrel Sends a Friend
chapters.summary: POV Felix. An old smuggling contact, Dara, offers safe harbor — then reveals she's tracking Felix for Kestrel intelligence. Beat: betrayal, but Dara hesitates; even hunters have loyalties.

chapters.title: The Long Dark Between
chapters.summary: POV Ilya. Fading fast, Ilya recounts how he stole the key from the war's architects. Beat: elegy — a man spending his last days making sure truth survives him.

chapters.title: Gravity Remembers
chapters.summary: POV Wren. The nine-second flicker repeats, longer this time, and Wren discovers it follows the shard like a wake. Beat: wonder curdling into fear — the cargo is changing physics around them.

chapters.title: Vane's Open Hand
chapters.summary: POV Felix. A Vane admiral offers Felix citizenship, protection, riches — if she surrenders the shard. Beat: temptation; Felix almost says yes, then hears the colony laughing in the galley.

chapters.title: Dara's Choice
chapters.summary: POV Dara. Torn between orders and old friendship, Dara warns Felix of an ambush instead of springing it, and defects mid-chase. Beat: the price of survival paid by someone else first.

chapters.title: The Ambush at Serpent's Coil
chapters.summary: POV Felix. Both fleets corner them in an asteroid shoal. The navigator's treason charts buy an escape through unmapped space. Beat: terror and exhilaration; the colony fights as one body.

chapters.title: Wreckage of the First Day
chapters.summary: POV Felix. In unmapped space they find the derelict where the war began — and the shard resonates, replaying the full truth: a weapons test disguised as an attack. Beat: grief and fury.

chapters.title: Ilya's Last Transmission
chapters.summary: POV Ilya. Ilya dies with the decryption complete, leaving Felix his memories and a message: 'Truth is cargo too. Deliver it.' Beat: mourning; inheritance made literal.

chapters.title: The Split
chapters.summary: POV Wren. The crew fractures: deliver the truth publicly and risk everything, or sell it quietly and live. Wren, youngest, argues loudest for delivery. Beat: found family tested by fear.

chapters.title: Hunted Through the Shallows
chapters.summary: POV Felix. A relentless pursuit through gravitational shallows; the medic is wounded shielding Wren. Beat: guilt — Felix sees her caution has a body count.

chapters.title: The Neutral Station
chapters.summary: POV Felix. They reach Meridian Station, where the war's architects still dine above the fighting. Felix realizes the truth must be delivered here, in front of everyone. Beat: resolve hardening into purpose.

chapters.title: Broadcast from the Vault
chapters.summary: POV Felix. Using Ilya's key and the station's ancient array, Felix broadcasts the first-day recording to every fleet, every world. Beat: climax — exposure, alarms, guns drawn, and silence spreading outward.

chapters.title: What the Fleets Did Next
chapters.summary: POV Dara. On opposite ships, soldiers watch the same truth. Some stand down; some don't. Dara talks her own captain out of firing on Meridian. Beat: fragile, human hope amid chaos.

chapters.title: Ceasefire at Nine Seconds
chapters.summary: POV Felix. Hostilities pause — not peace, but a held breath. The architects are arrested by their own officers. Gravity flickers once more, nine seconds, like a signature. Beat: exhausted awe.

chapters.title: Inheritance
chapters.summary: POV Wren. The colony buries Ilya in the station's memorial ring. Wren inherits his spare lace and his logs. Beat: bittersweet continuity — the dead pass their cargo on.

chapters.title: The Long Route Home
chapters.summary: POV Felix. Felix flies the colony toward a small moon nobody claims, where they might build something. She keeps one memory from the vault: Ilya's sunrise. Beat: quiet joy — invisible no more, and glad of it.
